b: I don’t know if you’re superstitious or not, but many people have a thing about the number 13 and Fridays that fall on the 13th day of the month. Sooo…

For today’s prompt, write a luck poem. Could be good luck, bad luck, or luck that is in some kind of gray area. Maybe it’s finding a lucky penny (something I did often as a youngster), or perchance having a lucky time of day or song or shirt or (fill-in-the-blank). And if you don’t believe in luck, well, you’re in luck, because you can write about that too today. Yes, anti-luck poems are considered luck poems by me (because why not).
Remember: These prompts are springboards to creativity. Use them to expand your possibilities, not limit them.

Here’s my attempt at a Luck Poem:

Is it lucky if you get lost
but eventually find your way,
or does it count against the cost?
Is it lucky if you get lost
even if every bridge you crossed
added more wonder to your day?
Is it lucky if you get lost
and eventually find your way?
(Note on today’s form: Today, I wrote a poem using the French form triolet. Also, I just realized I was wearing my “Lucky Shirt” today, which is kind of funny.)
When you realize you’re wearing your “Lucky Shirt” while writing a luck poem.
